title: re-announce drain loop POSTs to stale roots on root flap
description: Security review of 99sg.2 (pass 2, finding 2): node.py _reannounce_capabilities_to_new_root iterates ALL drained transitions (for _previous, new_root in changes). On a root flap (A->B->A, up to ROOT_CHANGE_HISTORY_MAX=8 entries) the node sends signed capability statements to roots it no longer belongs to — including a briefly/adversarially joined DODAG — disclosing capabilities to unintended parties and burning LoRa airtime. Only the latest new_root is the current root and needs the announcement.
close_reason: FIXED on beads-worker-4: _reannounce_capabilities_to_new_root now announces only to the newest drained DODAGID (changes[-1]) instead of every queued transition; earlier flap entries are superseded history and no longer receive signed capability statements. Guard reordered to 'not changes or capabilities == 0' (fixes the empty-queue IndexError the reorder initially exposed); drain still precedes the capabilities==0 early-return so silent nodes never leak ledger entries. Regression test test_root_flap_announces_only_to_current_root (A->B->A flap queues 2 transitions, exactly 1 POST to A). Verification: 7/7 reannounce tests + 140 node tests pass; ruff check/format clean; mypy clean. 3x codereview (kimi): correctness PASS, security PASS, robustness PASS with one P4 doc nit (docstring still said 'each new root') — corrected inline in this same diff since it was introduced by this fix.
